name: Scenario 1: Possible Account Compromise
description: Unusual login from unmapped geographical IP (185.44.21.8) on new device DEV099, followed by 5 failed login attempts, successful login, sensitive database access to SRV012, suspicious PowerShell execution, privilege escalation, and outbound connection to 185.44.21.8.

name: Scenario 2: Lateral Movement Chain
description: Lateral movement chain hopping across internal hosts: USR205 -> DEV020 -> 172.16.4.25 -> SRV003 -> SRV008 -> SRV014 with WMI admin enumeration and Kerberoasting ticket reuse.

name: Scenario 3: Suspicious Data Exfiltration
description: Abnormal off-hours activity from unrecognized device DEV088, multiple failed logins, mass file read operations on SRV004, tarball archive compression, and outbound exfiltration stream to 91.22.18.4.

name: Scenario 4: Ransomware Staging & Prep
description: Phishing lure execution spawning wscript.exe, execution of vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet to inhibit system recovery, rapid connection to backup storage SRV015, and file renaming loop.

name: Scenario 5: Malicious Insider Threat & Data Theft
description: Midnight off-hours login by sales employee, privileged database dump of 25,000 enterprise client records from Customer-DB-11 (SRV011), and synchronization to personal cloud storage.

name: Scenario 6: Cloud API Credential Leak & IAM Abuse
description: Leaked AWS long-term access key used from foreign IP 194.26.29.112, automated S3 bucket enumeration, rogue AdministratorAccess IAM policy attachment, and mass secret bucket dump.
expectedPattern: Cloud API Credential Leak & IAM Abuse

name: Scenario 7: Password Spray & Tor Exit Brute-Force
description: High-velocity password spraying bursts originated from known Tor Exit Node 185.220.101.5 resulting in eventual unauthorized access and SUID discovery binary execution.

name: Scenario 8: Supply Chain Package Poisoning & C2
description: Malicious npm postinstall dependency triggering interactive reverse shell back to 45.154.255.89, continuous C2 heartbeat beaconing, and injection into CI/CD build pipelines.
expectedPattern: Supply Chain Package Poisoning & C2 Beaconing

name: Scenario 9: Cryptojacking & Resource Hijacking
description: Unauthorized deployment of xmrig cryptocurrency mining binary on GPU cluster SRV016 masquerading as systemd service, establishing stratum mining pool telemetry on port 3333.

name: Scenario 10: Privilege Escalation & Domain Takeover
description: Exploitation of local sudoers vulnerability on SRV013, unauthorized promotion into Enterprise Admin group, and ntdsutil active directory snapshot dump.

name: Scenario 11: Normal Corporate User Baseline (Sales)
description: Standard daily employee workflow during normal business hours (09:00 - 17:30) using recognized company laptop DEV002, internal IP 10.10.20.12, and Okta SSO push notification MFA.

name: Scenario 12: Normal Corporate User Baseline (Engineer)
description: Routine developer workflow with hardware FIDO2 MFA token verification, GitHub repository clone, kubectl log review on staging cluster, and Jira ticket updates.

name: Scenario 13: False Positive Audit Pass (Pre-Approved Window)
description: IT Engineer performing scheduled end-of-month audit access to SRV012. Session is authenticated via primary device DEV003, verified with MFA_SUCCESS, and authorized under change ticket CHG-8821.
expectedPattern: Verified Legitimate Sensitive Access (False Positive Pass)

name: Scenario 14: Blended Enterprise Day Shift (Multi-User Concurrent)
description: Full concurrent corporate log set containing events from 6 distinct users (normal workflows, false positive maintenance, and active attacks from Rahul, Priya, Vikram). ThreatLens AI automatically sorts and prioritizes the threats.
